messages:
sam-cs: Hey team — we've been getting a bunch of 500s and huge tail latency this morning. Our app sets region=eu-west-1 but I see requests hitting us-east-1 in our logs. Can you check routing?

maria-support: Sorry you're seeing that, sam. Do you have a request id or example timestamp? Also, any client-side header that pins region?

sam-cs: example req id: req_20260317_4321. From our side the SDK init uses region: "eu-west-1" and endpoint https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate. Quick curl that failed: 

```bash
curl -i -X POST \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-xxxxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Response: HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error, then lots of 504s. Latency ~1.5s -> 8s on retries.

maria-support: thanks. pinging @kevin-sre and @jessica-infra to check routing and region capacity.

kevin-sre: I see the trace for req_20260317_4321. The request was routed via eu-west-1 origin, then proxied to us-east-1 due to region-drain policy on the eu-west-1 pool. There was a spill to another region because the eu-west-1 queue hit max_backlog. That matches cross-region hops and the extra latency.

jessica-infra: confirm — eu-west-1 had capacity exhaustion on GPU pool eu-west-1a at 08:42 UTC, autoscaled but backlog triggered our cross-zone fallback policy. Normally that fallback chooses eu-central-1, but routing rules allowed us-east-1 as a lower-cost fallback for this account because of tier mapping; that caused token-scope/auth mismatch for some requests.

sam-cs: token-scope/auth mismatch? We didn't change keys. We got 401s intermittently as well.

kevin-sre: Right. Some customer API keys are scoped to region-specific KMS/HSMs for compliance. When requests are proxied cross-region, our auth service rejects if token scope doesn't include the target region. That shows up as 401s mid-retry and then client libs retry and hit 500/504 cascades.

maria-support: Is there a quick workaround we can give the customer to stop cross-region routing and force eu-west-1 until we stabilize capacity?

jessica-infra: Yes — they can pin region in request header X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 or set the SDK's region option to strict_region=true (server will reject fallback if not allowed). For immediate mitigation, we can also add a per-account routing override to prefer eu-central-1 instead of us-east-1.

sam-cs: thx. Do we need any creds rotation? The 401s look scary.

kevin-sre: No rotation required. Those 401s were caused by mismatch when the request ended up in a region whose KMS didn't recognize the token. Once pinned back to eu-west-1 (or allowed eu-central-1), auth is fine. We'll follow up with a list of affected keys.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-43 — region fallback causing cross-zone auth errors and increased latency. Assigned to kevin-sre.

maria-support: Sam, for repro steps for internal escalation we need: 1) sample curl + request-id (you gave one), 2) client region header + SDK config, 3) timing window (approx 08:40-09:05 UTC), 4) whether you saw 401 then 500 or 500 then 401. Can you confirm 4?

sam-cs: Confirmed sequence was: initial 500, retry -> 401, retry -> 504.

kevin-sre: Notes for path to fix:
- Short term: apply account-level routing override to ban us-east-1 as a fallback and prefer eu-central-1. Also suggest customer set X-Redwood-Region header.
- Medium: increase reserved capacity on eu-west-1 pool for 2 hours to drain backlog and avoid future automatic spill.
- Long term: tighten fallback mapping to avoid cross-continent fallbacks for region-scoped tokens; add a KMS-aware routing decision.

jessica-infra: I'm pushing the override now and kicking a temporary scale-up. ETA 5m to policy update, 12m for instances to become available.

billing-bot: FYI — account had a sudden burst that exceeded soft quota; if they continue heavy traffic we will hit a billing throttle which can cause 429s. We sent a quota warning at 08:35 UTC.

sam-cs: We did a traffic spike from a batch job by mistake, that's probably it. We'll throttle back and keep region pinned. Appreciate the fast response. :pray:

maria-support: Follow-ups: kevin will post postmortem and list keys affected; jessica will confirm when override/scale complete; billing will confirm quota state after customer throttles.

kevin-sre: Override applied at 08:50 UTC, scaling started. Observed eu-west-1 backlog drop by 70% at 09:00 UTC. Will collect metrics and attach to INC-2026-0317-43.

jessica-infra: Scale completed at 09:02 UTC. Routing policy enforced; no more cross-region hits for sam-cs after 09:05 UTC.

billing-bot: Quota reset recommendation sent to customer at 09:07 UTC.

sam-cs: Confirming behaviour returned to normal ~09:06 UTC. Will monitor and escalate if we see more. Thanks all :heart:
